label: late copy-phase input of o / c / t (/ w)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input token is o, c, t or w (99.8% of activations; o 48% of mass, c 34%, t 15%, w 4%). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on any other input token. Rate rises steeply with position: almost nothing before recall_idx 3, and most mass at recall_idx 5-8 / t 14-17, so long sequences (L=8-9) dominate. Magnitude is largest when the next output is also from the o/c/t cluster or a digit (e.g. c->o, o->o, c->t). Restricting out_tok to that cluster raises precision to about 0.33-0.37 but drops recall to about 0.45. Even late in the sequence, most o/c/t/w copy inputs stay inactive (precision about 0.07), so some further context gates it that I could not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: o, c, t, w, a, -; least: p, g, f, s) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: o, t, c, 3; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
